root_cause.text: The SOCKMAP subsystem fails to strip SCM attributes (including inflight file descriptors and associated references) from AF_UNIX skbs before enqueuing them into the psock internal queue, allowing the GC’s assumption that all inflight sockets are reachable via the socket graph to be violated and leading to use-after-free when a freed socket is later accessed by the GC.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: “SOCKMAP can hide inflight fd from AF_UNIX GC” and “SOCKMAP redirect breaks the Tarjan-based GC's assumption that unix_edge.successor is always alive, which is no longer true once skb is redirected, resulting in use-after-free.” The patch introduces `unix_orphan_scm()` which calls `scm_stat_del()` and `unix_destruct_scm()` and changes the destructor to `sock_wfree` before passing the skb to the recv_actor, thereby dropping all SCM attributes before SOCKMAP handles the skb.

Attaches file descriptors to the skb as SCM credentials, creating the inflight references that are later not stripped before enqueuing into the psock queue, directly contributing to the GC violation.

Sets the destructor that should clean up SCM attributes when the skb is freed, but if the skb is enqueued into psock and its lifetime extended, this destructor may not be called in time, leaving dangling references.

Destroys the SCM cookie in the destructor; again, this is deferred and does not strip attributes before the skb enters the psock queue, allowing use-after-free conditions to arise.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement passes the skb (which still contains SCM attributes including inflight file descriptors) to the recv_actor callback without stripping the attributes. The recv_actor then enqueues the skb into the psock internal queue, violating the GC's reachability assumption and leading to use-after-free.

This statement retrieves an AF_UNIX skb that contains SCM attributes (including inflight file descriptors) from the socket's receive queue. The skb is then passed to recv_actor without any stripping of those attributes, directly enabling the vulnerability.

This statement attaches SCM file descriptors to the skb, creating the inflight references that must be later stripped before the skb is enqueued into the psock queue. Failure to strip these references allows dangling pointers that the GC will mistakenly treat as reachable.

This statement sets the skb's destructor to unix_destruct_scm, which is supposed to clean up SCM attributes when the skb is freed. However, if the skb is enqueued into the psock queue and its lifetime is extended, this destructor may not be called in time, leaving inflight references dangling and causing use-after-free.

This statement is part of the destructor unix_destruct_scm; it detaches the SCM file descriptors from the skb. But because the destructor is only invoked when the skb is freed, and the skb may be held indefinitely in the psock queue without being freed, this cleanup does not occur in time to prevent the GC from accessing freed sockets.

This statement is also part of the destructor; it destroys the SCM cookie and associated resources. It is deferred until skb free, but in the vulnerable scenario the skb remains alive and the inflight references persist, allowing a use-after-free when the GC later walks the socket graph.
